items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for the managed fleet; blocked for SearchWoot public beta or go-live. The security baseline covers 59 sites but reports no completed fleet-doctor run, no checks, and no operational deploy/uptime/error sweep. Authentication boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release controls, dependency risk, data exposure, incident signals, and disclosure readiness are therefore unverified—not clean. No TLS certificates are reported as expiring within 30 days. Recommend preserving the private gate and authorizing only bounded read-only evidence capture.

The four reversible SEO changes may proceed conditionally as ordinary low-risk work, subject to existing factual, disclosure, rollback, and measurement controls. Security evidence does not support blocking ordinary growth solely for optional hardening. Do not treat the changes as security-reviewed go-live or deployment approval.

SearchWoot remains blocked for public exposure. Existing evidence confirms an API access mechanism but not redistribution rights, while privacy, retention, vendor, incident, accuracy, attribution, measurement, and security-release gates remain incomplete. An unsent permission request is safe to prepare, but must not be sent without owner approval.
